Flagged as moderately uncertain since only 1-2 samples per second were available.

eye_and_blink_notes: Across all 12 periodic frames both characters keep their eyes open with a heavy-lidded, half-closed upper lid and a fixed forward/off-screen gaze (toward an implied TV). No blink is captured in any sampled frame, and pupil position barely shifts between frames, reinforcing a static, glassy, 'checked-out' stare consistent with the 'low battery' concept of the series.
head_movement_notes: Head position and tilt are essentially locked across the sequence; camera and character poses in periodic-0 through periodic-9 are nearly identical. The only visible variation is a very slight downward chin tilt on the man in periodic-3/4/6/7 versus periodic-0/1/2, likely tied to speech emphasis rather than a deliberate head turn. No pan, dolly, or character head rotation is evident.
gesture_notes: Both characters keep their hands folded/resting in their laps in the same position in every sampled frame - the woman's hands stay clasped together, the man's forearms stay resting on his knees. No hand raise, point, or other gesture occurs anywhere in the periodic sample, keeping the body language completely flat and inert throughout the joke.
idle_motion_notes: Aside from the felted-fiber shader giving a faint frame-to-frame shimmer to the sweater and suit surfaces, there is no visible idle motion: no breathing sway, no weight shift, no cloth settling, and no secondary motion in the woman's loose hair strands or the man's ears/collar. The near-total physical stillness of both puppets across the whole runtime is used as the comedic device (matching the 'low battery' premise), with only the mouths and captions carrying the scene.
frame_rate_feel: Metadata reports 30fps. The sampled periodic frames (roughly one per second over the 11.6s clip) show smoothly progressing, non-repeating mouth shapes tracking the dialogue with no evidence of duplicated or strobing frames, suggesting the piece is animated at or near full frame rate rather than posed on 2s/3s stop-motion holds. Combined with the almost frozen body poses, the overall feel is less 'choppy stop-motion' and more like a static illustrated tableau with smooth lip-sync layered on top.
overall_animation_style_notes: A single locked-off, deadpan sitcom-couch composition carries the entire clip: two long-nosed felt-shaded CG puppets sit motionless in front of a rainy night-city window while word-by-word captions ('get', 'home?', 'No.', 'I', 'you') appear beneath them in sync with a short, deadpan exchange. Bookend title cards ('Episode 43' cold-open corner label, a bold yellow 'SHE SAID NO' headline mid-scene, and a closing 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / CREATED BY NIN.' card with a 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' badge) do most of the narrative lifting, with the character animation itself limited almost entirely to lip movement and fixed heavy-lidded expressions rather than full-body performance.
